content:
maria: Quick flag — after the kernel-selection rollout last night I see a solid uptick in per-token 99p latency for the long-context routes. Dashboards show a gap around 03:15–03:45 UTC. Anyone digging in?

alex: Yep, noticed that on the token-latency breakdown. The increase is in the 'compute' and occasionally in 'kv_cache_lookup' when context > 8k. 99p went from ~220ms -> ~480ms on those routes.

sasha: I profiled a few slow traces, uploaded a flamegraph: https://git.redwood/infer/pg/flamegraphs/178400-profile.svg  Main hotspot seems to be kernel selection + a fallback path that re-reads KV cache metadata.

observability-bot: alert: token_latency.99p > 400ms (route=long-context) — triggered 2026-03-10T03:20:12Z.

samir: I have a hunch: when we switched default kernel heuristic it increased the number of kernel-compatibility checks for longer seqs. That added extra round trips in the runtime which inflate compute timing and also sometimes race with KV cache refreshes.

jenny: Also seeing some missing datapoints for token_latency.* in the OTLP sink between 03:10–03:30. There are gaps in per-route KPIs (route=long-context and route=webhook-batch). Might be exporter-side.

alex: Replaying statsd export logs — the OTLP exporter kept transiently failing gRPC streams and our retry backoff currently drops metrics after 5 failed batches. I can reproduce locally with a high-cardinality route tag storm.

maria: So two problems: (1) runtime perf regression due to kernel selection change, (2) metrics dropped in pipeline during the same window. We need to triage both but they are related.

samir: Quick triage notes:
- Kernel path: added extra `probe_kernel_compat` loop in PR #4821. On long sequences the loop runs up to 3 attempts before choosing a fallback kernel. That explains added compute.
- KV cache: `kv_meta_refresh` was scheduled synchronously when we picked fallback kernel; should be async.
- Exporter: OTLP client had `max_concurrent_streams=8` default; under high tag cardinality streams saturated and exporter returned UNAVAILABLE, after N retries our StatsD shim drops.

sasha: Proposed short fixes:
1) Revert the extra probe loop in PR #4821 (hotfix).
2) Make `kv_meta_refresh` async and only refresh on confirmed kernel switch.
3) Increase OTLP `max_concurrent_streams` to 32 and bump buffer sizes in statsd->otlp bridge.

maria: Can we hotfix (1) immediately and run a small canary? Deploy-bot, can you queue a rollback PR for #4821 canary?

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback PR #4821-canary -> staging. ETA ~8 minutes. CI checks running.

alex: I pushed a patch to the exporter config here: https://git.redwood/infer/ops/otlp-configs#increase-streams diff includes `max_concurrent_streams: 32` and `batch_bytes_limit: 262144`

jenny: For the missing metrics we'll need a backfill. I sketched a backfill plan: run metrics-backfill job for `token_latency` and `kv_cache_hit` from 2026-03-10T03:00Z to 2026-03-10T04:00Z, grouped by `route` and `kernel_variant`. Command: `./tools/metrics-backfill --metric token_latency --from 2026-03-10T03:00Z --to 2026-03-10T04:00Z --group-by route,kernel_variant --dest metrics-archive`

samir: Careful — backfill will double count if some downstream aggregators already consumed partial data. We should mark backfilled series with tag `backfill=true` and ensure analytics queries exclude them by default.

sasha: I'll run the backfill in the dry-run mode first and post the sample output. Plan: dry-run now, then real backfill after we confirm exporter stability.

maria: Timeline:
- 03:30 — rollback canary (rolling)
- 03:38 — verify token_latency dashboards for drop in 99p
- 03:45 — re-deploy exporter config (alex)
- 03:50 — dry-run backfill (sasha)
- 04:00 — real backfill if dry-run looks good (sasha + jenny)

alex: Noted. I also opened a follow-up PR to add telemetry around kernel probe iterations: `runtime.kernel.probe_count` (gauge) and `runtime.kernel.fallback_reason` (tagged). PR #4827.

jenny: After backfill we should run a regression eval against the same prompt set used in the rollout. If latency improves but quality changes, we need to revert kernel heuristic permanently.

sasha: dry-run results: no duplicate series in sample, backfill payload size ~12MB for the hour, command: `./tools/metrics-backfill --dry-run ...` — looks safe.

deploy-bot: rollback PR #4821-canary applied to staging; health checks passing.

observability-bot: notice: token_latency.99p returned to baseline (~230ms) for route=long-context in staging at 2026-03-10T03:39:12Z.

maria: Good. alex, proceed with exporter config rollout after staging verification. Sasha/jenny coordinate real backfill at 04:00. Add a short postmortem note once done.

samir: I'll follow up with a small runtime change to make kernel probe bounded and non-blocking. Planning a proper fix for next patch.

jenny: I'll schedule a postmortem and add the backfill tagging conventions to the runbook.

maria: Thanks all — great cross-team moves. :thumbsup: Keep updates here until complete.
